name: Stirling-PDF
description: #1 PDF Application on GitHub that lets you edit PDFs on any device anywhere
readmeExcerpt:
Stirling PDF - The Open-Source PDF Platform

Stirling PDF is a powerful, open-source PDF editing platform. Run it as a personal desktop app, in the browser, or deploy it on your own servers with a private API. Edit, sign, redact, convert, and automate PDFs without sending documents to external services.

## Key Capabilities - **Everywhere you work** - Desktop client, browser UI, and self-hosted server with a private API. - **50+ PDF tools** - Edit, merge, split, sign, redact, convert, OCR, compress, and more. - **Automation & workflows** - No-code pipelines direct in UI with APIs to process millions of PDFs. - **Enterprise‑grade** - SSO, auditing, and flexible on‑prem deployments. - **Developer platform** - REST APIs available for nearly all tools to integrate into your existing systems. - **Global UI** - Interface available in 40+ languages. For a full feature list, see the docs: **https://docs.stirlingpdf.com** ## Quick Start ```bash docker run -p 8080:8080 docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf ``` Then open: http://localhost:8080 For full installation options (including desktop and Kubernetes), see our [Documentation Guide](https://docs.stirlingpdf.com/#documentation-guide). ## Resources - [**Documentation**](https://docs.stirlingpdf.com) - [**Homepage**](https://stirling.com) - [**API Docs**](https://registry.scalar.com/@stirlingpdf/apis/stirling-pdf-processing-api/) - [**Server Plan & Enterprise**](https://docs.stirlingpdf.com/Paid-Offerings) ## Support - **Community**: [Discord](https://discord.gg/HYmhKj45pU) - **Bug Reports**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/issues) ## Contributing We welcome contributions! Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines. This project uses [Task](https://taskfile.dev/) as a unified command runner for all build, dev, and test commands. Run `task dev` to get started running the editor, run `task` to see the most common commands, or see the [Developer Guide](docs/developer/DeveloperGuide.md) for full details. For adding translations, see the [Translation Guide](docs/developer/HowToAddNewLanguage.md). ## License Stirling PDF is open-core. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.
readmeHtml:
Stirling PDF - The Open-Source PDF Platform

Stirling PDF is a powerful, open-source PDF editing platform. Run it as a personal desktop app, in the browser, or deploy it on your own servers with a private API. Edit, sign, redact, convert, and automate PDFs without sending documents to external services.

Key Capabilities

  • Everywhere you work - Desktop client, browser UI, and self-hosted server with a private API.
  • 50+ PDF tools - Edit, merge, split, sign, redact, convert, OCR, compress, and more.
  • Automation & workflows - No-code pipelines direct in UI with APIs to process millions of PDFs.
  • Enterprise‑grade - SSO, auditing, and flexible on‑prem deployments.
  • Developer platform - REST APIs available for nearly all tools to integrate into your existing systems.
  • Global UI - Interface available in 40+ languages.

For a full feature list, see the docs: https://docs.stirlingpdf.com

Quick Start

docker run -p 8080:8080 docker.stirlingpdf.com/stirlingtools/stirling-pdf

Then open: http://localhost:8080

For full installation options (including desktop and Kubernetes), see our Documentation Guide.

Resources

  • Documentation
  • Homepage
  • API Docs
  • Server Plan & Enterprise

Support

  • Community: Discord
  • Bug Reports: GitHub Issues

Contributing

We welcome contributions! Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines.

This project uses Task as a unified command runner for all build, dev, and test commands. Run task dev to get started running the editor, run task to see the most common commands, or see the Developer Guide for full details.

For adding translations, see the Translation Guide.

License

Stirling PDF is open-core. See LICENSE for details.

releases.name: 3.5.0 New Conversions are Live! and Desktop reload fix and more
releases.body:
Stirling Office Convert has now replaced Libreoffice in our docker containers! 
Along with speed increases and better quality conversions it also means our docker going forward in 3.5.1 will be half the size!  Thank you to everyone who sent us example files, and please keep reporting any conversions that don't look right! We are hoping to get this perfect!

We have also made a big fix for desktop users whose documents were reloading a few seconds after upload, Thank you to everyone who reported this and great to see people using the new feedback button! (In bottom right) 

With the Office Convert change (outside of the tools getting the toggle removed)
- Compress now uses Office Convert
- HTML to PDF supports zoom again
- New admin setting to cap how many Office conversions run at once and queue
- Damaged Office, ebook and HTML files now give a clear "could not be read" message instead of an error

Other changes are:
- Faster desktop PDF operations, with the PDF engine now pre-installed in the app
- Performance improvements across the viewer, file list etc
- JPDFium and other dependency updates causing various bug fixes and improvements 

We also fixed some bugs inc

releases.name: 3.4.0 Big text editor changes, OneDrive, SCIM and Accessibility checker
releases.body:
A big release!  Lots of changes in this release around the PDF Text Editor, such as it now works directly inside the viewer by clicking the edit text button in the top bar. 
Other changes for it include: 

- It can use fonts from the server including any custom provided fonts that are placed in customFiles/static/fonts/.
- It does a much better job of matching scanned (OCRed) documents to their fonts
- Brand new font picker for those OCR scenarios
- General text editor fixes for typed text and lag issues
- Embedded fonts are now subset, so saved files are smaller.

Other features in this release include: 
- OneDrive support has been added to our pro plan with more to come soon
- Brand new check PDF accessibility tool which checks PDFs against PDF/UA-1 or PDF/UA-2 and generates reports (More to come soon!)
- New setup wizard for new server setups to help onboard users easier 
- Enterprise users get SCIM 2.0 user provisioning
- Admins concerned about users editting and invalidating signatures can now disable users from doing that, this also comes with a new signature detection interface

Other changes are:
- New settings menu submenu with easy access logout button

releases.name: 3.3.0 Conversion upgrades, bug fixes and several minor improvements
releases.body:
Stirling Office Convert (still beta) has been upgraded. You can also now pick it as the converter in lots of other tools such as Email, HTML, Markdown and ebooks to PDF plus PDF to HTML/Markdown/XML/EPUB/AZW3, and PDF/A. Please compare it with the existing converter and let us know!

Our roadmap is to turn Office Convert on by default next week, and then, if no changes are required, fully remove LibreOffice and other dependencies the week after. So now is the best time to try it and report (And send example files) any conversions that don't look correct!

Other changes are:
- SSO auto-login now works even when username/password login is enabled (admins can still reach the password form via /login?all)
- JPDFium upgrade and support and Windows ARM64 support, This update also brings better redaction, merge/split improvements and lower memory on big files 
- Faster and more accurate mobile scanning, with no more 9MB OpenCV bundled
- Faster requests with far fewer database reads and new entity caching
- Quieter startup and runtime logs
- Spring Boot, Docker base image and lots of other dependency updates
- Updated translations for all languages

We also fixed some bugs inc

releases.name: 3.2.2 new annotations and other minor changes and improvements
releases.body:
Another small release with some bug fixes

- Fix for some viewer rendering issues 
- New auto fit to width button for viewer
- New annotation shape options like arrow and polyline
- QR code stamp types

## What's Changed
### Bug Fixes
* fix(i18n): expand Turkish translations by @alkank in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8123
* fix(viewer): render non-embedded fonts with matching widths by @reecebrowne in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8629
### Enhancements
* feat(viewer): Fit to width and fit to page buttons in the viewer by @EthanHealy01 in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8485
* Fix race condition in storybook by @jbrunton96 in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8619
* build(deps-dev): bump fast-uri from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9 in /frontend by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8580
* build(deps-dev): bump ip-address from 10.7.2 to 10.7.4 in /frontend by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8630
* build(deps): bump dompurify from 3.4.16 to 3.4.17 in /frontend by @dependabot[bot] in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PD

releases.name: 3.2.1 Viewer improvements and bug fixes
releases.body:
Smaller release with some nice viewer and editor improvements and bug fixes for annotation and compression

Key features  are:
- Arrow key support for viewer
- Dual page view to support cover pages
- Read aloud now starts at the selected text
- You can now duplicate pages in page editor (multi tool)
- Memory optimisations
- Label damaged PDFs and offer Repair
- Export PDF comments as CSV


Bug fixes
- Fixed cases were compression was not correctly compressing
- Fixed various annotation issues introduced in 3.2.0 
- Fixed issues with default tool picker mode

<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at main -->

## What's Changed
### Bug Fixes
* fix: persist Default tool picker mode and Default view on launch settings by @mvanhorn in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/6827
* fix(annotate): transparent shape fills and hollow default shapes by @reecebrowne in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8574
* fix(viewer): exit annotation mode when the toolbar button is clicked again by @balazs-szucs in https://github.com/Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF/pull/8590
### Enhancements
* Update Backend 3rd Party Lic

aiSummary.oneLiner: A comprehensive, self-hosted open-source platform offering deep PDF manipulation and conversion tools without externa...
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Stirling PDF is a highly capable open-source document manipulation platform that empowers users to perform comprehensive edits, conversions, and automation on PDF files locally. It operates primarily as a Dockerized web application, ensuring sensitive documents are fully processed locally without ever pinging external cloud services for heightened data security. The platform consolidates a massive array of utilities, allowing users to effortlessly merge, split, OCR, digitally sign, and deeply redact dense multi-page documents directly from their browser. By exposing a completely private internal API, developers can also seamlessly integrate complex PDF processing routines into their own self-hosted automation pipelines.
keyFeatures: Total Privacy: Ensures all document processing, OCR, and redaction happens completely locally on your hardware without external API calls.
Comprehensive Editing Toolset: Enables deep structural changes to files including merging, splitting, signing, and granular page reordering.
Advanced OCR Integration: Converts scanned images into fully searchable and selectable text documents seamlessly using localized processing.
Private Developer API: Exposes a comprehensive local web API allowing complex PDF transformation routines to be automated securely.
Multi-Environment Deployment: Supports running natively as a desktop application, directly in the browser, or as a self-hosted Docker container.
Extensive Format Conversion: Converts documents fluidly back and forth between PDF and numerous image, word, or structured text formats.

useCases.title: Secure Document Redaction
useCases.description: Legal professionals utilize the platform to completely locally redact sensitive personal information from case files without trusting cloud converters.

useCases.title: Automated OCR Pipelines
useCases.description: Developers deploy the Docker container to automatically ingest and parse incoming physical scans using the exposed local API.

useCases.title: Enterprise Document Standardization
useCases.description: Host the application internally to provide all staff with a robust, highly secure unified PDF editor.

useCases.title: Rapid Batch Processing
useCases.description: Archivists utilize the comprehensive merging and splitting tools to organize and rapidly catalog massive historical document libraries offline.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Privacy-conscious individuals, enterprises, and developers who need a powerful, fully locally-hosted solution for managing and editing PDF files securely. It is suitable for professionals looking for efficiency.
